findings.evidence: Lines 189–191 give `isSpectralMap_eval i` under `∀ j, j ≠ i → IsCompact univ`, while lines 212–219 strengthen this to compactness of every factor solely to discharge that hypothesis.
findings.fix: Replace `[∀ i, CompactSpace (Z i)]` with `hZ : ∀ i j, j ≠ i → IsCompact (univ : Set (Z j))` and pass `hZ i` to `isSpectralMap_eval`; optionally derive the current compact-factor form as a corollary if needed.
findings.issue: `IsProConstructible.pi` assumes every `Z i` is compact, but `isSpectralMap_eval` at line 189 only requires compactness of the other factors; for a singleton index, the product is just `s i` and needs no compactness assumption.

summary: The arbitrary-product theorem imposes unnecessary compactness in the singleton-index case despite the preceding evaluation theorem already exposing the exact weaker hypothesis.
